dhp235:1: You are now like a withered leaf,
dhp235:2: Yama’s men stand waiting for you,
dhp235:4: with no provisions for the journey found.
dhp236:1: One should make an island for oneself,
dhp236:2: soon the wise one should endeavour,
dhp236:4: you will go to the divine and noble realm.
dhp237:1: You are now advanced in age,
dhp237:2: you have come to Yama’s presence,
dhp237:3: there is nowhere to dwell in between,
dhp237:4: with no provisions for the journey found.
dhp238:1: One should make an island for oneself,
dhp238:2: soon the wise one should endeavour,
dhp238:4: you will not come to birth and old age again.
dhp239:2: little by little, moment by moment,
dhp239:3: should remove the stain from himself,
dhp239:4: like a smith (removes the stain) from silver.
dhp240:1: As a (rust) stain arises from iron,
dhp240:2: and arisen from that, it eats it away,
dhp240:3: so with one who is overindulgent –
dhp240:4: his deeds lead him to a bad destiny.
dhp241:1: Lack of repetition is the ruin of chants,
dhp241:2: a lack of maintenance is the ruin of homes,
dhp241:3: indolence is the ruin of one’s appearance,
dhp241:4: heedlessness is the ruin of the one on guard.
dhp242:1: Bad conduct is a woman’s stain,
dhp242:4: both in this world and in the next.
dhp243:1: A stain that is worse than that stain,
dhp244:1: Life is light for one without shame,
dhp244:2: with the bold courage of a crow,
dhp245:1: Life is hard when endowed with shame,
dhp245:2: for the one constantly seeking purity,
dhp245:3: for one sincere, and not reckless,
dhp246:2: and speaks a word that is not true,
dhp246:3: takes what is not given here,
dhp247:1: that person who is devoted to a drink of liquor and wine,
dhp247:3: digs up his own root right here in the world.
dhp248:2: a lack of restraint is a bad thing,
dhp248:3: let not greed and corruption oppress you with suffering for a long time.
dhp249:1: The people give according to faith,
dhp249:3: herein the one who becomes dejected
dhp249:4: because of food and drink (given) to others
dhp249:6: either by day or nigh attain to (good) concentration.
dhp250:1: For the one in whom this (dejection) is cut off,
dhp250:2: destroyed at the root, dug up,
dhp250:3: does, by day and night, attain to (good) concentration.
dhp251:1: There is no fire that is like passion,
dhp251:2: there is nothing that takes a hold like hatred,
dhp251:3: there is no snare like delusion,
dhp251:4: there is no flood like craving.
dhp252:1: Easy to see are others’ fault,
dhp252:2: but one’s own is hard to see,
dhp252:3: for one sifts other people’s faults like they were chaff,
dhp252:6: like a crafty cheat (conceals) his defeat.
dhp253:1: The one who constantly looks for another’s fault, who is an abject complainer,
dhp253:4: he is far from their destruction.
dhp254:1: There is no footprint in the sky,
dhp254:2: there is no ascetic on the outside,
dhp254:4: the Realised Ones are free of impediments.
dhp255:1: There is no footprint in the sky,
dhp255:2: there is no ascetic on the outside,
dhp255:4: there is no disturbance for the Buddhas.
dhp255:5: The Chapter about Stains, the Eighteenth Warding off wickedness one is called a brahmin, one living austerely is said to be an ascetic, * because of driving forth (all) stain from oneself one is said to be one who has gone forth.
